newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai feed mills sidelined by high grain prices.
newsitem.headline: Thai feed mills sidelined by high grain prices.

text.p: The Thai grain and oilseed market was quiet this week despite stronger demand as buyers were sidelined by recent high international prices, trade sources said on Tuesday.
Importing activity was thin. The prices of soymeal and corn in the local market rose amid tighter supplies, the sources told Reuters.
But traders expected buying to emerge if international prices continued to ease, following a drop last night in reaction to a bearish crop estimate report from the U.S. Agriculture Department.
"The prices eased last night due to the news. If they continue their downward momentum a bit, buyers could enter the market again very soon," said one trader from a U.S. trading house.
One major oil crusher expressed interest in buying around 50,000 tonnes of soybeans but had not concluded the deal due to high prices.
Tight soymeal supplies were partly offset by arrivals from India and product crushed from imported beans.
Soymeal prices were quoted around 9.60 baht ($0.36) a kg from 9.55 baht last week.
The market welcomed Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee's comment that he would consider allowing zero-tariff corn imports by mid-March.
However, since no further details were available, buyers took a wait-and-see stance.
Traders said the ministry should come up with details soon as local corn stocks were depleting.
Active local buying pushed the corn price up to 4.50 baht a kg from 4.30-4.40 baht last week.
Industry sources projected that they would need to import up to 400,000 tonnes of corn this year.
